newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call rate softens after Buba adds funds.
newsitem.headline: German call rate softens after Buba adds funds.

text.p: German call rates eased on Tuesday after the Bundesbank injected a surprisingly large 1.6 billion marks into the banking system via its securities repurchase, or repo, allocation.
The overnight call rate slipped to 2.95 percent from around three precent on Monday. Traders said they expected the rate to slip further toward 2.90 percent this afternoon.

The Bundesbank left the market with ample funds this morning, awarding 62.2 billion marks in repos at the same time that only 60.6 billion marks were expiring. Traders had expected the Bundesbank to drain a small amount of funds.
Traders said the Bundesbank's decision to add funds showed the central bank did not want the call rate to shoot too high at the end of the month.
The call rate often climbs sharply at the end of the month as banks scramble for funds to meet month-end reserve requirement targets.
Traders also said the injection meant that banks probably would not be forced to borrow too much from the emergency Lombard lending facility which carrys a 4.50 percent interest rate.
Banks held 41.9 billion marks with the Bundesbank on Monday, up slightly from 41.8 billion marks on Friday. The average for the month as of Monday stood unchanged at 40.8 billion marks.
Banks borrowed no appreciable amount of funds from the Lombard lending facility on Monday.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average on Monday stood at 2.98676 percent vs 3.03267 percent on Monday.
